questions.prompt: What does the TestScheduler give you for testing time-based streams?

options.text: A controllable virtual clock so delays resolve instantly and deterministically
A way to run Observables on a web worker

questions.explanation: The TestScheduler runs scheduled work on virtual time, so operators like debounceTime and delay complete immediately and predictably instead of using slow, flaky real timers.

questions.prompt: Inside `testScheduler.run()`, how much virtual time does one frame (one marble character) represent?
questions.explanation: Within run(), 1 frame = 1 ms, and each character advances the virtual clock by one frame. Use time-progression syntax like '10ms a' for larger gaps.

questions.prompt: In a marble diagram, what does `#` represent?
questions.explanation: `#` is an error, `|` is completion, `()` groups same-frame emissions, and `^` marks a hot observable's subscription point.

questions.prompt: How do you map marble letters like `a` and `b` to real emitted values?

options.text: Pass a values object, e.g. expectObservable(x).toBe('-a-b|', { a: 1, b: 2 })
You cannot; letters always emit themselves as strings only
By naming them in the TestScheduler constructor
By using numbers instead of letters in the marble

questions.explanation: A values map translates marble characters into real values. Without it, `a` emits the string 'a'.

questions.prompt: All marble helpers (cold, hot, expectObservable) must be used inside this TestScheduler method. Type its name (no parentheses).
questions.explanation: testScheduler.run(callback) supplies the helpers and auto-virtualises the schedulers, so time-based operators are driven by virtual time.

questions.prompt: In an `expectSubscriptions` diagram, what do `^` and `!` mean?

options.text: ^ marks when the source was subscribed; ! marks when it was unsubscribed
^ marks an error; ! marks a completion
^ marks the first value; ! marks the last value

questions.explanation: Subscription diagrams use ^ for the subscribe frame and ! for the unsubscribe frame — useful for verifying cancellation (e.g., switchMap unsubscribing a previous inner).
